items.title: Beijing Foresky Community Center / PLAT ASIA
items.summary: The project is situated in the Foresky Community on the South Fourth Ring in Beijing , surrounded by parks. It serves as a community center that fosters a shared living place—a communal space among neighbors. Its design is based on the concepts of Gathering and Return, which focus on spatial experience.

items.title: Casa Circular / efcarquitetura
items.summary: The architectural design of the Casa Circular was developed in response to its owners' demands for an accessible residence, without stairs or elevators, including the desire for a rooftop garden.

items.summary: Australian studio Casey Brown Architecture has created two Corten cabins in New South Wales, that reference the silhouette of pitched tents.

items.title: MVRDV tops "polite yet radical" Eindhoven housing with angular roofs
items.summary: A cluster of housing blocks with jagged grass-covered rooftops form Nieuw Bergen, a residential complex completed by Dutch studio MVRDV in Eindhoven.

items.title: G-Beach Residence / B+D+M Architetti
items.summary: The G-Beach Residence project originates from the dialectical relationship between the existing Hotel Bellevue, designed by Renzo Menegazzo in 1956, and the surrounding pine forest. The hotel building references the Belo Horizonte Library designed by Oscar Niemeyer in 1955, adopting its main architectural features.

items.title: Sydney Harbour Bridge Cycleway Ramp / ASPECT Studios
items.summary: The Sydney Harbour Bridge Cycleway Ramp redefines access to one of Australia's most significant pieces of public infrastructure. For decades, the northern approach to the Bridge's cycleway ended in stairs, breaking one of the city's most iconic journeys.

items.title: La Piada / pfeffermint AG

items.title: Candy Loft / SUSA
items.summary: Delivered in Spring 2025, this residential renovation within Toronto's historic Candy Factory Lofts reinterprets a 1907 confectionery plant as a contemporary home shaped by layers of industrial, cultural, and spatial memory.

items.title: When Façades Become Habitats: Architecture Making Room for Other Species
items.summary: When we think of façades , we rarely think of them as habitats. We see them as the elements that separate interior from exterior, regulate temperature, reduce noise, and protect buildings from external conditions.

items.summary: The project originated as a response to Shenzhen's high-density urban environment. As a city rapidly built from reinforced concrete, Shenzhen's spatial experience often exhibits a highly ordered, industrialized character.
